name: Barf Green
lede: Barf Green is a sharp, acid yellow-green named for vomit, one of a loose family of bodily-fluid names the 2010 xkcd color survey gave to this part of the green-yellow range.

sections.title: A crowd name for a bodily comparison
sections.body:
The name comes from Randall Munroe's 2010 xkcd color survey, where visitors typed a word next to a swatch and the most common label for each cluster of clicks won [1]. Who typed "barf green" first is undocumented; the survey records only the winning name [1]. ISCC-NBS 1955 would file the same patch as a strong yellow green, about 5.4 units off, with Munsell notation 3.9GY 6.5/10.1 [1].

The closest look-alikes in our data are [[pea-soup-green|Pea Soup Green]], 2.1 units away and duller, and [[sickly-green|Sickly Green]] and [[booger-green|Booger Green]], both almost the same shade, with [[avocado-green|Avocado Green]] a duller neighbor [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive of 23,781 paintings, as photographed, finds this acid green in only 6 of them, about 0.03 percent, rarer than 75 percent of our named colors [2]. The handful of matches include a work by Odilon Redon, dated 1888, with the latest match from 1941; the sample is too small here for a reliable century or role breakdown [2]. As with most of this family of vivid yellow-greens, its rarity in old paint likely reflects how few historical pigments could produce it cleanly [2].
